horizon_driver: gold and SIP holdings are multi-year/retirement-oriented for the formal-sector subset; effective horizon shortens sharply for the large informal-labour and remittance-dependent subset, which behaves closer to HH_EM_URBAN/HH_EM_SUBSIST

constraints.action: abandon gold as a savings vehicle in favour of fully formal financial assets
constraints.source: gold's cultural/wedding-linked demand and its function as a state-independent store of value
constraints.breaks_under: a sustained real-return gap strongly favouring formal equity/debt with no rupee-depreciation or informal-economy risk

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Indian gold demand is traditionally framed as jewellery/cultural (weddings, festivals) rather than financial.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Q1 2026 investment demand (bars/coins) rose 54% YoY to 82 tonnes while jewellery volumes fell 19% YoY even as jewellery spending rose 47% (price-driven, not volume-driven); investment demand then cooled to 54t in Q2 2026 from a ~100t/quarter run-rate, tracking the gold-price and hedging cycle rather than the wedding calendar. Total 2024 demand was 802.8 tonnes, making India the world's second-largest gold consumer.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The actor is increasingly treating gold as an investment/FX-hedge instrument rather than primarily a cultural purchase, confirming the Cartographer's 'private decentralised FX reserve' framing.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Mutual-fund industry messaging in 2025-26 frames SIP retail investors as a stable, uniformly 'sticky' long-term domestic equity bid.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Net SIP inflows hit a record ~₹2 trillion in FY26 (Apr 2025-Mar 2026) with successive record monthly contributions (₹29,361cr Sep-25, ₹31,002cr Dec-25, ₹31,961cr Jul-26) even as SIP account closures rose during 2025-26 market turbulence, and active SIP accounts still grew past 10 crore.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The aggregate flow is a genuine, near-mechanical record bid supporting the 'forced flow' framing, but it masks rising account-level churn — headline stickiness is partly a composition effect (new accounts replacing closed ones), not universal individual discipline.

tripwires.if: the rupee depreciates sharply or the gold price spikes further (e.g., a geopolitical or dollar-funding shock)
tripwires.then: investment-demand gold buying accelerates further even as jewellery volumes keep falling — the jewellery/investment bifurcation widens rather than aggregate gold demand simply rising

tripwires.if: domestic equity indices see a sustained (2+ quarter) double-digit drawdown
tripwires.then: SIP account closures accelerate materially beyond the FY26 rate, testing whether net SIP inflows can stay positive

what_would_change_my_mind: A quarter where investment gold demand falls together with a stable or strengthening rupee (i.e., gold buying decouples from the hedging motive) would undercut the 'private FX reserve' framing. Note: the informal-labour-supply and remittance-receipt sub-controls in the Cartographer file were not independently sourced in this pass and remain thin evidence.
